question: Who promoted the worship of God in Punjab, India as Nirankar (Formless)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Baba Dayal Das.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baba Dayal Das** promoted the worship of** God in Punjab**, India as** Nirankar.**
 
• Nirankar is a term used in Sikhism to describe **God as formless **and **beyond human comprehension.**
 
• The concept of Nirankar is central to **Sikhism** and is one of the key beliefs of the religion.
 
• The term Nirankar is derived from the Sanskrit word "**nirankara**" which means** "without form".** 
 
• In Sikhism, the worship of God as Nirankar emphasizes the importance of** inner devotion and spiritual growth **rather than external rituals and ceremonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Gobind Singh** was the **tenth Sikh guru** who is known for his role in** shaping the Sikh religion** and creating the **Khalsa Panth. **
 
• **Baba Ram Singh** was a **19th century Sikh leader** who led a rebellion against the British colonial government.
 
 
• He was known for his efforts to promote **Sikh nationalism and social reform.**
 
 
 
• **Maharaja Ranjit Singh **was a **Sikh ruler **who established the Sikh Empire in the** 19th century.**
 
 
• He was known for his** support of Sikhism** and his efforts to promote the religion.
